pr_body:
This removes the default implementation of `getMinimalSupportedVersion`
and implements it in all `NameDiffs` implementations.

The default implementation was rather broad, `minimumIndexCompatibilityVersion`
as the index compatibility are wider than our wire compatibility.
Having a default implementation also had the implementors forget about
adjusting the wire compatibility to the correct version.

This should be back-portable back to `7.16` with a few minor changes (and 
the main branch will have to remove some extra `7.x` references in a follow-up).
Minimising the scope for errors when reviewing was the purpose of still referencing 
`7.7` (for eg) in the main branch. 

Fixes #81262

issue_context.title: Custom metadata diffs must override `getMinimalSupportedVersion()`
issue_context.body:
**Elasticsearch version** (`bin/elasticsearch --version`): 7.9 through 7.16. Unsure why it didn't reproduce on 7.7 and 7.8, it looks like these overrides were necessary but omitted there too.

**Plugins installed**: []

**JVM version** (`java -version`): Anything

**OS version** (`uname -a` if on a Unix-like system): Anything

**Description of the problem including expected versus actual behavior**:

In https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/issues/81110 we saw publications failing with the older node reporting an `Unknown NamedWriteable` called `component_template`:

```
[2021-11-30T23:28:26,300][WARN ][o.e.c.c.PublicationTransportHandler] [v7.4.0-2] unexpected error while deserializing an incoming cluster state |  
-- | --
  | »  java.lang.IllegalArgumentException: Unknown NamedWriteable [org.elasticsearch.cluster.NamedDiff][component_template] |  
```

That's true, this was introduced in 7.7 so we shouldn't even be sending it to 7.4 nodes. It's confusing, however, because these objects return the right version from `getMinimalSupportedVersion()` which should be removing them from the cluster state that's sent to the old nodes.

It turns out that the problem is that these objects also implement a custom diff mechanism and the resulting diff object does _not_ override `getMinimalSupportedVersion()`. The fix is something like this:

```diff
diff --git a/server/src/main/java/org/elasticsearch/cluster/metadata/ComponentTemplateMetadata.java b/server/src/main/java/org/elasticsearch/cluster/metadata/ComponentTemplateMetadata.java
index 95b6d0bb794..92fe6f18f9b 100644
--- a/server/src/main/java/org/elasticsearch/cluster/metadata/ComponentTemplateMetadata.java
+++ b/server/src/main/java/org/elasticsearch/cluster/metadata/ComponentTemplateMetadata.java
@@ -164,5 +164,10 @@ public class ComponentTemplateMetadata implements Metadata.Custom {
         public String getWriteableName() {
             return TYPE;
         }
+
+        @Override
+        public Version getMinimalSupportedVersion() {
+            return Version.V_7_7_0;
+        }
     }
 }
diff --git a/server/src/main/java/org/elasticsearch/cluster/metadata/ComposableIndexTemplateMetadata.java b/server/src/main/java/org/elasticsearch/cluster/metadata/ComposableIndexTemplateMetadata.java
index 374d19cb573..1b5193510aa 100644
--- a/server/src/main/java/org/elasticsearch/cluster/metadata/ComposableIndexTemplateMetadata.java
+++ b/server/src/main/java/org/elasticsearch/cluster/metadata/ComposableIndexTemplateMetadata.java
@@ -165,5 +165,10 @@ public class ComposableIndexTemplateMetadata implements Metadata.Custom {
         public String getWriteableName() {
             return TYPE;
         }
+
+        @Override
+        public Version getMinimalSupportedVersion() {
+            return Version.V_7_7_0;
+        }
     }
 }
```

However I haven't done an exhaustive search for all the places where this override is missing.

**Steps to reproduce**:

 1. Start up a 7.6.2 single-node cluster.
 2. Add a master-eligible 7.16.0 node to this cluster.
 3. Exclude the 7.6.2 node from the voting configuration using `POST _cluster/voting_config_exclusions/<node_name>`. This causes it to abdicate to the 7.16.0 node which will then send it a cluster state containing unknown customs.

**Provide logs (if relevant)**:

```
[2021-11-30T23:28:26,300][WARN ][o.e.c.c.PublicationTransportHandler] [v7.4.0-2] unexpected error while deserializing an incoming cluster state |  
-- | --
  | »  java.lang.IllegalArgumentException: Unknown NamedWriteable [org.elasticsearch.cluster.NamedDiff][component_template] |  
  | »  	at org.elasticsearch.common.io.stream.NamedWriteableRegistry.getReader(NamedWriteableRegistry.java:112) ~[elasticsearch-7.4.0.jar:7.4.0] |  
  | »  	at org.elasticsearch.common.io.stream.NamedWriteableAwareStreamInput.readNamedWriteable(NamedWriteableAwareStreamInput.java:45) ~[elasticsearch-7.4.0.jar:7.4.0] |  
  | »  	at org.elasticsearch.cluster.NamedDiffableValueSerializer.readDiff(NamedDiffableValueSerializer.java:56) ~[elasticsearch-7.4.0.jar:7.4.0] |  
  | »  	at org.elasticsearch.cluster.NamedDiffableValueSerializer.readDiff(NamedDiffableValueSerializer.java:30) ~[elasticsearch-7.4.0.jar:7.4.0] |  
  | »  	at org.elasticsearch.cluster.DiffableUtils$MapDiff.<init>(DiffableUtils.java:406) ~[elasticsearch-7.4.0.jar:7.4.0] |  
  | »  	at org.elasticsearch.cluster.DiffableUtils$ImmutableOpenMapDiff.<init>(DiffableUtils.java:234) ~[elasticsearch-7.4.0.jar:7.4.0] |  
  | »  	at org.elasticsearch.cluster.DiffableUtils.readImmutableOpenMapDiff(DiffableUtils.java:127) ~[elasticsearch-7.4.0.jar:7.4.0] |  
  | »  	at org.elasticsearch.cluster.metadata.MetaData$MetaDataDiff.<init>(MetaData.java:873) ~[elasticsearch-7.4.0.jar:7.4.0] |  
  | »  	at org.elasticsearch.cluster.metadata.MetaData.readDiffFrom(MetaData.java:812) ~[elasticsearch-7.4.0.jar:7.4.0] |  
  | »  	at org.elasticsearch.cluster.ClusterState$ClusterStateDiff.<init>(ClusterState.java:883) ~[elasticsearch-7.4.0.jar:7.4.0] |  
  | »  	at org.elasticsearch.cluster.ClusterState.readDiffFrom(ClusterState.java:793) ~[elasticsearch-7.4.0.jar:7.4.0]
```

review_comments:
@droberts195 I've made some changes for ML too. The `minimalSupportedVersion` refers to wire-compatibility, so it should never be `minimumIndexCompatibilityVersion` (as the index BWC guarantees are wider than the wire ones).
Let me know if this doesn't make sense to change as part of this effort?

Thanks for changing it.  I think what was there before worked by fluke because the effective constraint was what you're allowed to run at all in a mixed version cluster.  `MlMetadata` has existed back to 5.4, so this effective constraint never resulted in sending incorrect diffs to a node that wouldn't understand them.  (I am assuming we had `Version.V_5_4_0` here in 5.4, 5.5 and 5.6, and even if we didn't it's way too late to change it.) But still, it's good to have the correct constant here for the future.

In 7.16 `IndexLifecycleMetadata#getMinimalSupportedVersion()` returns `Version.V_6_6_0`. Obviously this is earlier than `Version.CURRENT.minimumCompatibilityVersion()` but still it would be good to return the same value in both places when backporting.
